source: Typical savings ranges compiled from US DOE / ENERGY STAR / ASHRAE efficiency-measure guidance — international benchmark ranges, not Singapore-metered results. Each range is the measure's saving as a % of the energy used by its own end-use category (e.g. a refrigeration measure's % is of refrigeration energy, not total electricity). Air-side economizers/free-cooling are intentionally excluded — not applicable to Singapore's tropical climate. `certainty` ("high" = hardware/capital measure with a fixed physical effect; "variable" = controls/software/behavioral measure whose realized saving depends on ongoing configuration and use, per site-visit feedback that BMS/setpoint-type savings are not guaranteed) and `effortTier` ("low"/"medium"/"high" implementation effort/disruption, distinct from cost) were added this phase to support ROI+effort-based ranking and honest confidence labeling — both are judgement calls made from the same evidence base, not separately re-sourced. Two chiller-plant measures (`high-efficiency-chiller-replacement`, `chiller-plant-optimization-controls`) were added 2026-09-24 to close a gap for commercial-building clients (Office/Professional Services, Retail, Hospitality, Healthcare) whose HVAC bill is chiller-plant-dominated — previously only fan/pump VSDs and generic BMS scheduling covered the HVAC end-use, with no measure addressing the chiller itself.

measures.label: LED lighting retrofit
measures.evidence: US DOE — LED retrofits typically cut lighting energy 30-60% vs. fluorescent/incandescent baselines.

measures.label: Occupancy sensors & daylight harvesting controls
measures.evidence: US DOE — occupancy and daylight-linked lighting controls typically save a further 10-30% of lighting energy on top of the fixtures themselves.

measures.label: Variable-speed drives on HVAC fans & pumps
measures.evidence: ASHRAE / US DOE — VSDs on HVAC fans and pumps typically cut that equipment's energy 20-50%, roughly 10-30% of total HVAC energy.

measures.label: BMS-based scheduling & setpoint optimization
measures.evidence: US DOE — BMS-based scheduling and setpoint optimization typically saves 5-15% of HVAC energy with no new capital equipment.

measures.label: High-efficiency chiller plant replacement
measures.evidence: ASHRAE / US DOE — replacing an aging constant-speed chiller plant with high-efficiency (VSD/magnetic-bearing) chillers typically cuts chiller energy 20-30%, the single largest lever in a commercial building's HVAC bill in a cooling-dominant climate like Singapore's.

measures.label: Chiller plant optimization (sequencing, condenser water reset)
measures.evidence: ASHRAE Guideline 36 / US DOE — optimized chiller sequencing and condenser water reset controls typically save 8-15% of HVAC energy without new chiller hardware; realized saving depends on ongoing commissioning and tuning, same caveat as other controls-only measures.

measures.label: Refrigeration controls & floating head pressure
measures.evidence: ASHRAE / US DOE — floating head pressure and refrigeration controls typically cut refrigeration energy 8-15%.

measures.label: Door strip curtains & open-door alarms on walk-in coolers
measures.evidence: ENERGY STAR — door strip curtains and open-door alarms typically save 3-6% of refrigeration energy by cutting infiltration.

measures.label: Night covers on open refrigerated display cases
measures.evidence: ENERGY STAR grocery guidance — night covers on open display cases typically save 2-5% of refrigeration energy.

measures.label: High-efficiency refrigeration compressor replacement
measures.evidence: ENERGY STAR — replacing aging refrigeration compressors with high-efficiency units typically saves 10-20%.

measures.label: Demand-controlled kitchen exhaust hoods
measures.evidence: US DOE / ENERGY STAR — demand-controlled kitchen exhaust hoods typically cut associated fan energy 20-30%, roughly 10-20% of total cooking-area energy.

measures.label: ENERGY STAR certified cooking equipment
measures.evidence: ENERGY STAR — certified commercial fryers, griddles and ovens typically use 10-20% less energy than standard models.

measures.label: Compressed air leak survey & repair
measures.evidence: US DOE — compressed air leak surveys and repair typically recover 5-10% of system energy (leaks commonly waste 20-30% before repair). Recurring maintenance action — savings depend on repeating the survey, not a one-off capital fix.

measures.label: Variable-speed drives on process motors, pumps & fans
measures.evidence: US DOE — VSDs on motor-driven pumps, fans and compressors typically cut that equipment's energy 15-25%.

measures.label: Waste heat recovery on process equipment
measures.evidence: US DOE — waste heat recovery on industrial process equipment typically saves 5-12% of process energy.

measures.label: Laundry / drain-water heat recovery
measures.evidence: ENERGY STAR hospitality guidance — drain-water and laundry heat recovery typically saves 10-20% of laundry energy.

measures.label: Low-flow fixtures & hot water system optimization
measures.evidence: ENERGY STAR — low-flow fixtures and hot water system optimization typically save 10-20% of hot water energy.

measures.label: Hot/cold aisle containment
measures.evidence: Huawei / Eaton data centre efficiency guidance — hot/cold aisle containment typically cuts cooling energy 10-25%.

measures.label: High-efficiency UPS replacement
measures.evidence: Data centre efficiency guidance — replacing older UPS units with high-efficiency (>97%) models typically cuts UPS losses 20-40%.

measures.label: Server virtualization & consolidation
measures.evidence: Common data centre efficiency practice — virtualization/consolidation typically cuts IT load energy 10-30% by raising utilization.

measures.label: Dock door seals & loading-bay air curtains
measures.evidence: US DOE warehouse guidance — dock door seals and air curtains typically save 5-10% of material-handling-area energy via reduced infiltration.

measures.label: Sterilizer / autoclave cycle batching & scheduling
measures.evidence: Healthcare energy management guidance — batching and scheduling sterilizer/autoclave cycles typically saves 5-10% of associated energy.

measures.label: Plug load management (smart strips, PC power management)
measures.evidence: US DOE — plug load management typically saves 10-20% of plug load energy.

measures.label: Sub-metering & power-quality monitoring
measures.evidence: Cross-portfolio benchmark — sub-metering and power-quality monitoring typically surfaces 5-10% waste via anomaly detection by enabling further optimization, not by directly reducing load itself.
